c.tagline: City of pearls and biryani, where Nizami palaces meet the glass towers of HITEC City.

taxi.fareNote: Auto-rickshaws are metered by law but drivers often quote a flat fare, so agree the price or insist on the meter before starting; app cabs (Uber/Ola) and Rapido bikes are usually cheaper and hassle-free.

emergency.note: 112 is India's unified single emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance; 108 is the free ambulance service and 100 the police helpline.

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing is common in the crowded Charminar/Laad Bazaar lanes and on buses; avoid poorly lit Old City backstreets late at night.

hood_desc: The historic heart of Hyderabad around the 1591 Charminar, Mecca Masjid, Chowmahalla Palace, and the bangle-lined Laad Bazaar; crowded and chaotic but unbeatable for monuments, pearl and bangle shopping, and legendary Old City biryani.

An upscale district of designer boutiques, fine-dining restaurants, rooftop bars, top hospitals, and the leafy Road No. 1 and Road No. 12; suits travelers who want comfort, shopping, and nightlife close together.

A posh residential-and-entertainment area home to film celebrities, the forested KBR National Park, trendy cafes, clubs, and the Jubilee Hills Check Post; good for upscale dining and stylish nightlife.

Hyderabad's modern IT corridor of glass office towers, malls like Inorbit and Sarath City, business hotels, breweries, and coworking spaces around Cyber Towers and the Financial District; the convenient base for tech and business travelers.
The colonial twin city with a cantonment feel, the landmark Clock Tower, Parade Ground, and the main railway junction; more local, calmer, and easier on the budget than central Hyderabad.

water.note: Tap water is not safe for visitors; use bottled or filtered water, including for brushing teeth.

transit.hours: Hyderabad Metro runs roughly 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM; TSRTC city buses run from early morning to around 11:00 PM, with app cabs and autos filling late-night gaps.
transit.note: Hyderabad Metro Rail is one of India's largest metro networks, with three lines (Red, Blue, Green) spanning about 69 km; it is complemented by TSRTC city buses and the MMTS suburban rail.
transit.pay: Buy paper QR/token tickets at metro counters or use the T-Savaari app and rechargeable smart cards; city buses take cash or the same smart card. UPI/QR payment is widely accepted.

bus: Intercity buses from MGBS (Imlibun) and JBS (Jubilee) bus stations
train: Secunderabad, Nampally (Hyderabad Deccan), and Kacheguda railway junctions

transit.m: Pushpak AC Airport Liner bus (TSRTC) to Secunderabad, HITEC City, and other hubs (~60-90 min)
Uber/Ola cab to city center (~45-60 min); a metro Airport Express line to Raidurg is under construction

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving ~5-10% at restaurants and ₹20-50 for hotel porters or valet service is appreciated.
